history.summary: A Śvetāmbara Jain temple complex at Badridas Temple Street, Gouribari/Maniktala, North Kolkata, built in 1867 by Ray Badridas Bahadur Mookim; consecration (pratishtha) performed by Sri Kalyansurishwarji Maharaj. The complex holds four temples: the main shrine to Shitalanatha (10th Tirthankara), whose seated idol's diamond-studded forehead is a noted attraction; the Chandraprabha shrine south of it, built 1895 by Ganeshlal Kapoorchand Jahar; a Mahavira shrine; and the Dadawadi housing the footprints of Acharyas Jinadattasuri (1075-1154 CE) and Jinkushalsuri. Celebrated for mirror-inlaid pillars, Belgian stained glass, marble floral inlay, chandeliers, gardens, fountains and a stream; a ghee lamp in the sanctum is said to have burned continuously since 1867. NAMING CONFLICT: the temple is called 'Pareshnath/Parshwanath' but the main shrine is dedicated to Shitalanatha (some sources say Parshvanath, 23rd Tirthankara - verify). NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - a Jain shrine; keep-or-drop decision needed.

name: Pareshnath Jain Temple
town_description: Kolkata, capital of West Bengal on the east bank of the Hooghly river, is India's cultural capital and a major metropolis with deep colonial history and religious diversity. The temple stands at Badridas Temple Street, Gouribari, in North Kolkata's Maniktala area.

travel.airport: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport, Kolkata (~15 km)
travel.railway: Kolkata railway station ~2 km; Sealdah nearby
travel.road: Badridas Temple Street, Gouribari/Maniktala, North Kolkata; cabs, autos and local transport available.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; early morning (6:00-10:00 AM) in summer.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM-12:00 PM and 3:00 PM-7:00 PM daily. Entry free; open to all religions. Food and drinks not allowed inside (verify). Paryushana (August-September) is the main festival period.
